title: repair_mesh touches only the regions it changes: one adjacency build, defect lists, patch orientation and intersection-curve pruning, cold under 1 s
user-messages:
> A redesign that stopped passing over the whole mesh in every stage, and touched only the regions that actually change, would remove most of the time. That’s a bigger change than the pruning redesign I described earlier.

lets plan for this
yes and stack the new ticket and get started on it after cleanup
description:
repair_mesh spends its time in whole-mesh passes while it changes only a few percent of a scan. Measured on the ten crawfish scans (CRAW-92 counters, about 1M faces each): orientation flips 0.05k-198k faces, the split touches 0.4k-8.8k vertices, degenerate collapse 4-59 faces, shell drop 0.2k-6.4k faces, fills add 1.6k-18.9k, pruning removes 1.5k-33k and refills 0.7k-13.6k. Yet every stage walks all faces, the edge table is rebuilt 8-11 times per repair, orientation casts parity for 76k-84k sample faces plus 68k-350k recast faces, and pruning round 0 re-examines every face (2.9k-31k full hemisphere casts). Cold, in a fresh JVM as the viewer first meets it, repair takes 3-5 s per scan; warm 0.9-1.85 s. Two thirds of the cold time is JIT warm-up, which grows with the number of distinct whole-mesh code paths.

Redesign the repair so only a handful of passes touch the whole mesh and every other stage works on the defects it was handed:

Whole-mesh passes that stay: read and weld; one adjacency build (vertex to faces, edge to corner uses), updated in place afterwards; one defect scan listing boundary, non-manifold and inconsistently wound edges, degenerate faces and components; one self-intersection search (one tree tested against itself); the output half-edge build from the working adjacency.

Stages on defect lists: split fans only at listed non-manifold vertices; collapse only listed degenerate faces; shells from the scan's components, containment rays only for large secondary shells; orientation per consistently wound patch from a few area-weighted ray samples, keeping the per-patch exposure-balance vote that fixed IMG_4113's eyes (CRAW-91); fills walked from the boundary-edge list and added to the adjacency in place.

Pruning by the mesh-arrangements idea: on a closed, consistently wound surface a face can show its back to the outside only where the surface crosses itself. Cut the surface into patches along the self-intersection curves, find the winding number behind each patch with a few rays, and drop patches with nothing solid behind them. Full hemisphere casts only where the winding is uncertain: faces beside intersection curves, slivers, tiny and creased faces. After a refill, test only the new fill faces against the mesh and reclassify only the patches they touch.

Read the mesh-arrangements paper's cell labelling before the pruning milestone; floating-point crossings on noisy scans will not be exact, so uncertain regions fall back to the hemisphere test rather than pretending to exact arithmetic.

Overlap: MESH-67 asks for repair under a second with output identical to today's; this ticket changes outputs (orientation and pruning decisions) and is judged by the zero-flip check instead.

Stacked on CRAW-92, whose zero-flip pruning stage, CrawfishOrientationCheckBenchmark and CrawfishColdRepairBenchmark this builds on.

Pruning, debris and fill measurements (cold, fresh JVM per scan; another process held about 4 of 16 cores throughout, load average 6 to 11).

GPU column parity (LWJGL GL 4.3 compute, integrated Radeon 860M): kernel 2 to 3.5 times faster than the CPU count once filtered (1M lines 120 to 216 ms, 75k lines 17 to 19 ms), but end to end only 0.15 to 0.25 s saved on IMG_4113 because the CPU still prepares the lines and the buffers are sent each pass; context creation 150 to 180 ms. Off by default; not worth landing on this machine.

Hemisphere blockers: a blocked face records the face that stopped each of its 25 rays and stays blocked while all of them stand (faces added later can only stop more rays). Identical exposed/pruned counts on all ten scans; saves about 80 ms on IMG_4113.

Loose-debris check: floods from the corners of the faces cut since the last check, settling per cut region, with a budget and an exact fallback to the whole-mesh check. Identical results on all ten scans; settles in 3 to 9 ms where it applies (5 of 10 scans) against 60 to 150 ms. Falls back whenever a loose piece of 100 faces or more needs the shell containment test (106 to 3,116 faces on 6 scans).

Exact minimum-area triangulation of large holes: the O(n^3) search is the floor (1,337-edge loop: about 470 ms single thread, 180 ms on all cores warm). A seeded bound, a block-diagonal schedule and chunked minima all gave identical triangulations and no speed-up, and were reverted.

Split large holes (result change): loops over 256 edges are cut along their shortest chord leaving at least a quarter of the loop on each side, each side searched the same way. 1,337-edge loop 290 to 57 ms, 851-edge loop 129 to 52 ms. Zero flips on all ten scans; face counts change on the scans with large holes (IMG_4113 pruning drops from 8 rounds to 4), so the goldens need a re-bless and the large patches a visual check.

Cold totals after these changes, all ten scans: 2,035 to 3,039 ms (average stages: prune 889, orient 642, assemble 354, fill 212, split 123, shells 86, read 47). GC pauses total about 60 ms per repair.
definition-of-done:
1. Cold repair_mesh (CrawfishColdRepairBenchmark: one fresh JVM per scan, the app's flags) under 1 s on all ten crawfish scans IMG_4109-IMG_4118, on a quiet machine, two runs each; warm times reported beside them.
2. CrawfishOrientationCheckBenchmark reports backOut=0, flaps=0, backSeen=0 on all ten scans.
3. The edge/adjacency structure is built once per repair; no stage rebuilds it.
4. A per-stage table of faces touched and time, before and after, for all ten scans.
5. MeshRepairTest, mvn test and the heavy goldens pass; any golden that changes is explained and re-blessed only with the user's agreement.
testing-plan:
1. After each milestone: MeshRepairTest, CrawfishOrientationCheckBenchmark on all ten scans, CrawfishColdRepairBenchmark on all ten scans.
2. Before review: mvn test and the heavy goldens (GoldenFingerprintTest -Dgroups=heavy).
3. Timings only on a quiet machine (load average under 2); note the load beside every timing table.
todos: DONE : M1 (done): edge table built once per repair and edited in place

DONE : M4 (replaced, done): intersection-curve pruning dropped after the probe (search cost more than it replaces); instead pruning rounds made local, later rounds judge only candidates, pruning reuses orientation's parity
DONE : M5: output half-edge mesh built from the edge table's two uses per edge instead of rehashing every edge; counting passes folded into the one write (identical output)

DONE : M2: one survey after the read (open, non-manifold and contested edge lists kept current; per-face normals and areas; slit and zero-area faces; one shared faces-around index); split, degenerates, fill, pruning setup (background tree, local creases) and debris driven by it (identical results)

DONE : M3: orientation per consistently wound patch, parity cast only round seams and folds; pruning round 0 from the same per-patch evidence (changes results: zero-flip check, goldens with the user's OK)

DONE : Hole triangulation (results-changing, beside M3, needs the user's go-ahead): MeshHoleFiller's minimum-area interval DP (Klincsek 1980; step 1 of Liepa 2003; area only, no dihedral term) is O(n^3) and dominates big holes: IMG_4117's 1337-edge loop 310 ms triangulating (refine 51, fair 43), IMG_4113's 851-edge loop 131 ms. Preferred fix: restrict the DP's candidate triangles to the loop's 3D Delaunay triangulation (Zou, Ju, Carr 2013, An algorithm for triangulating multiple 3D polygons), falling back to the full DP when that set holds no valid triangulation; near-linear in practice, same objective, may pick a different triangulation on irregular loops. Port from the paper only: CGAL's implementation is GPL. Other options weighed: split long loops at good chords then DP the pieces; ear clipping / advancing front (Zhao, Gao, Lin 2007), greedy and weaker on twisted loops; planar projection plus constrained Delaunay, fails on folded loops; volumetric fills, heavyweight. Fairing (bi-Laplacian, uniform umbrella, CG on normal equations, ring held fixed for tangent continuity) costs 5-45 ms per big hole and is left as is.
unknowns: How robust is self-intersection detection on noisy scans in floating point, and how wide must the hemisphere fallback band be?
Does per-patch orientation reproduce today's decisions on IMG_4113 and IMG_4117, the sensitive scans?
changes-made: M1 started: RepairEdges, an edge table built once with stable counting passes and edited per face (addFace, removeFace, find by lower vertex plus a chain for edges added later), with RepairEdgesTest checking that random removes, re-adds and turned faces leave the same uses as a fresh build. Next: port MeshRepair's stages onto it so no stage rebuilds the edges, and make the non-manifold split keep vertex ids (copies only for extra fans) so its edits stay local. Baseline logs (cold times, per-stage face counts, zero-flip check) copied to tmp/baseline.

M1 port: MeshRepair now keeps one RepairEdges table and re-files only the faces a stage touched (flips, detaches, collapses, shell drops, fills, pruning cuts, pinch splits, debris drops) instead of rebuilding the edge table 8-11 times per repair; only the non-manifold split, which still renumbers every vertex, forces one fresh build. MeshRepairTest, RepairEdgesTest, CoincidentAnchorSaveTest pass; IMG_4113, 4109, 4117 still 0/0/0 with identical exposed/pruned/rounds/refilled counts. Cold times (load average ~10, shared machine) before -> after: 4109 3.50->3.34 s, 4110 3.62->3.42, 4111 3.65->3.58, 4112 3.46->3.07, 4113 5.19->4.58, 4114 3.89->3.72, 4115 3.46->3.35, 4116 3.97->3.74, 4117 4.33->3.91, 4118 3.73->3.25. Next in M1: make the split keep vertex ids so that last rebuild goes too.

M1 done: the non-manifold split keeps vertex ids (each vertex's first fan keeps it, extra fans get copies and only their faces re-file), so the edge table is built exactly once per repair. mvn test 764 run, 0 failures; zero-flip check 0/0/0 on all ten scans. Hole discovery order follows vertex ids, so fills and pruning shift slightly: IMG_4113 exposed 3540->3554, pruned 33263->34889, rounds 6->8; other scans within about 2%. Cold (load average ~11) baseline -> M1: 4109 3.50->3.03 s, 4110 3.62->3.41, 4111 3.65->3.22, 4112 3.46->3.35, 4113 5.19->4.60, 4114 3.89->3.34, 4115 3.46->3.02, 4116 3.97->3.34, 4117 4.33->3.62, 4118 3.73->3.38.

Shell containment rays now read one column of the latest column grid (orientation's, then pruning's) plus a serial test of the faces added since, instead of a parallel pass over every face. Cold shells stage 325-525 ms -> ~52 ms; pruning's debris round on IMG_4109 422 -> 209 ms. Zero-flip check 0/0/0 on all ten scans with the same exposed/pruned/rounds as M1; MeshRepairTest passes. Cold stage times now (quiet machine, IMG_4109 / IMG_4113): read 47/57, orient 679/820, split 88/106, degen 30/45, shells 51/73, fill 176/510, prune 1442/3076, assemble 374/522; total 2.89 s / 5.22 s. Pruning is about half: setup (tree, columns, parity, creases) ~0.5 s, round 0 and 1 rays 110-365 ms each, IMG_4113 runs 8 rounds.

M4 probe (deleted after use, output in tmp/selfx.log): a parallel self-intersection search on repaired scans costs tree ~85 ms + search ~400 ms + patching ~60 ms warm on IMG_4109/4113/4117; crossing faces 974 / 10,399 / 2,842, leaving 50 / 614 / 183 patches. The search alone costs more than the per-face parity plus round-0 rays it would replace (~150-300 ms warm), so M4 as planned (pruning by intersection-curve patches) does not pay off; replanning pruning.

Voxel flood probe (deleted after use, logs tmp/voxel-IMG_*.log): unpruned mesh, triangles marked by their boxes, outside flood-filled, each face judged by the voxel one step behind it, checked against the 25-ray hemisphere test. Cold cost 150-230 ms at 256 voxels, 200-300 ms at 512. Decided enclosed (no rays needed): 50-57% of faces at 256, 40-49% at 512; the rest are open or sit in surface voxels. Wrong 'enclosed' verdicts (back actually visible): IMG_4109 0/0, IMG_4113 159/33, IMG_4117 2/1 at 256/512, from real gaps narrower than a voxel that the marked surface voxels close off. Not safe as a vouch on its own, and it decides fewer faces than the per-face parity does at a similar cost.

Pruning rounds made local (no decision changes): a vertex-to-faces index filed when pruning starts and chained as fills and pinch splits add corners drives ring growth, the kill, retiring, the cut's loop check (vertices numbered locally) and the pinch split; the companion tree is built over the added run only (TriangleBvh.firstTriangle); creases after a refill are judged from the faces round its corners; the refill reads only edges whose uses changed (RepairEdges tracks them; the table is brought current before each cut so a reopened side is seen), and its neighbour rows and mean edge lengths come from the faces round each boundary vertex, summed in edge order. Zero-flip check identical on all ten scans (same exposed/pruned/rounds), mvn test 764 pass. Cold (load ~8): IMG_4113 prune 3.08 -> 2.24 s, total 5.22 -> 3.96 s; IMG_4109 prune 1.44 -> 1.37 s; cut/refill/tree updates now 1-16 ms per round.

Pruning rounds after the first judge only candidate faces (no decision changes): faces whose evidence is not parity, faces added since the last round, parity-vouched faces whose line runs in a cell a changed face reaches (found by binary search in a (cell, face) list sorted once after round 0), and faces the last refill's crease check judged. Changed cells are now a sorted list (TriangleBvh.cellsUnder) instead of grid-sized flag arrays. All ten scans identical (0/0/0, same exposed/pruned/rounds/refilled), mvn test 764 pass. Cold (load ~9): IMG_4109 2.76 -> 2.52 s (prune 1.37 -> 1.17), IMG_4113 3.96 -> 3.59 s (prune 2.24 -> 1.86), IMG_4117 3.18 -> 3.17 s; later rounds on IMG_4109 ~100 -> 3-5 ms.

Pruning reuses orientation's parity (2026-11-02): right after orientation's flips, a background facing pass runs over orientation's column grid with the turned corners (TriangleBvh.withCorners, crowding margin set, line cells recorded) while split, degenerates, shells and fill run; pruning recasts parity only for faces touched since orientation (tracked in touch()), faces added since, and faces whose parity line runs in a cell those reach (2-12% of faces). The grid is only a filter, so the answers are the same floats. Crowding now ignores exposure-only fan triangles (no effect on pruning's soup). cellsUnder dedupes in place instead of a boxing IntStream.distinct. Verified: CrawfishOrientationCheckBenchmark identical on all ten scans (0/0/0, same exposed/pruned/rounds/refilled); mvn test 764 pass. Pruning setup wait 200-380 ms -> 44-190 ms; tree build 430-540 -> about 250 ms with the cores free; prune IMG_4109 ~1.05 -> ~0.83 s, IMG_4117 ~1.36 -> ~1.2 s, IMG_4113 unchanged (~1.9 s, its rounds dominate). Measured: a JDK 27 AOT cache trained on IMG_4110 cuts cold repair about 25-35% (IMG_4109 2.53 -> 1.76 s, IMG_4113 4.70 -> 3.52 s, IMG_4117 3.85 -> 2.67 s, three runs each); the first parity pass alone runs 4.5M column members in 199 ms interpreted versus 9.7M in 28 ms compiled. Not adopted: needs jar classpaths and a launch change, pending the user.
AOT cache rejected by the user (no compiler tricks); its training files are deleted and it is not pursued.

Plan (2026-11-02), user approved planning: one survey pass after the read (edge table plus kept-current lists of open, non-manifold and contested edges; per-face normals and areas; slit and zero-area faces; one shared faces-around index) and every stage works only on what it flags. Phase 1 keeps results identical: assemble from the edge table's twins, fill stage 6 on the open-edge list and near-only helpers, pruning's tree built in the background after orientation with retire plus companion, local non-manifold split and degenerates, orientation reading the survey, debris piece labels kept through cuts (last). Phase 2 changes results (per-patch parity in orientation and pruning round 0) and needs the user's go-ahead. Full plan in tmp/craw-93-survey-plan.md.

M5 (2026-11-02): assembly hands the half-edge build every corner's twin straight from the edge table (HalfEdgeMeshOps.buildFromIndexedMesh with cornerTwin; the old pairing by lower-vertex buckets moved to pairByLowVertex and still serves every other caller). An edge opens at its lower corner either way, so the mesh is the same id for id: checked array by array on IMG_4109/4113/4117 (2.8-2.9M half-edges each) and by the new KnownTwinsBuildTest. Zero-flip check identical on all ten scans; mvn test 765 pass. Cold assemble (load 9-10, two runs) 413/332/350 -> 306-316/263-284/276-340 ms on IMG_4109/4113/4117: corner checks plus pairing 165-170 -> 26-35 ms. What is left in assembly is filling the output's own arrays (130-175 ms: half-edge numbering, outgoing and vertex-face rows), normals (~45 ms) and the write (40-55 ms); the vertex rows can come from the shared faces-around index in M2.

M2 step, fill stage (2026-11-02): the faces-around index is filed once before stage 6 (not at pruning) and chained through fills and pinch splits; stage 6 reads mean edge lengths and neighbour rows off the faces round each boundary vertex (the near-only helpers pruning already used); the whole-mesh meanIncidentEdgeLength and buildVertexNeighbours are deleted; fillHoles takes openedByCuts for the changed-edge scan. Zero-flip check identical on all ten scans; mvn test 765 pass. Cold fill-stage whole-mesh work 55-75 -> 20-45 ms plus the index filing (14-19 ms, moved out of pruning's setup). What remains in stage 6 is the hole filling itself, dominated by MeshHoleFiller's cubic minimum-area triangulation on big loops: IMG_4117's 1337-edge loop takes 310 ms triangulating (refine 51, fair 43) and is the whole stage's wall time; IMG_4113's 851-edge loop 131 ms. Making that cheaper changes the fill triangles (a decision for the user).

M2 step, pruning setup (2026-11-02): orientation now also starts, in the background, a ray tree and the crease flags over its snapshot (turned corners, its positions and groups); pruning takes the tree over (TriangleBvh.adoptTree), retires every face touched since orientation and puts those still alive, with the faces added since, in the companion tree (treeOverFrom takes a list of extras below the run); crease flags are judged again only for faces round a vertex a face touched or added since used, before or after (creasesSinceOrientation; the whole-mesh pass is now the static creasedFaces over any snapshot; the refill path calls foldedBackNear directly). Zero-flip check identical on all ten scans; mvn test 765 pass. Pruning setup: tree 250-540 ms on the critical path -> companion 7-14 ms; creases 82-122 -> 13-55 ms. Cold (load ~6, two runs) IMG_4109 1.90/1.90 s (prune 0.58-0.60), IMG_4113 3.41/3.35 s (prune 1.62), IMG_4117 2.63/2.73 s (prune 0.87-0.98). The background work now overlaps the serial split and degenerate stages, which slow somewhat (split 72-109 -> 116-255 ms, degenerates 34-44 -> 61-96 ms). Remaining in pruning's setup: its own column grid (83-93 ms) and the parity patch (46-133 ms).

M2 step, split and degenerates (2026-11-02): the shared faces-around index is now filed right after orientation (not before the fill) and chained by the split, detach and collapse, which all give faces new corners. Degenerates: orientation records the faces its area loop finds exactly zero (flatFaces); the stage walks those in ascending order plus any face a collapse moves later in that order, reads faces round two vertices off the shared index (its own index and facesMovedTo map are gone). Split: a walk round each vertex across manifold edges, in parallel and allocation-free, shows one fan for nearly every vertex; only the rest are grouped (fansAt), extra fans get copies in the order the old walk over every corner met them and faces are touched in face order, so vertex ids and edge filing are unchanged; detach reads only the non-manifold edges found plus the edges a split re-filed. The background work orientation starts (parity, tree, creases) now runs on its own pool of half the cores (AHEAD_OF_PRUNING_POOL), so the stages in between keep the shared pool. Zero-flip check identical on all ten scans; mvn test 765 pass. Cold: degenerates 43-94 -> 0-2 ms; split's fan work 88-183 ms (union plus corner walk) -> 59-90 ms (one-fan walk), detach scan 16-25 -> 0-4 ms; split stage 115-182 ms including 0-100 ms re-filing orientation's flips.

M2 step, orientation (2026-11-02): turned faces are re-filed in place (RepairEdges.flipFace: each face keeps its three edges, the slots on its first and third sides trade places and every direction turns; RepairEdgesTest checks 400 random flips leave exactly the table remove-then-add leaves, edge ids included), so the split no longer re-files up to 200k flipped faces (0-100 ms -> 0-1 ms; the flips themselves 6-34 ms); the closed ray soup lists its open edges once instead of walking every edge three times (23-34 -> 16-20 ms); the faces-around index is filed inside orientation while its column grid finishes. Zero-flip check identical on all ten scans; mvn test 766 pass. Cold, two runs with GC logging (load 7-8; GC pauses 0.01-7 ms, not a factor): IMG_4109 1.90/1.97 s, IMG_4113 3.67/3.72 s, IMG_4117 3.04/2.92 s; stages IMG_4109/4113/4117 read 42-53, orient 583-776, split 59-159, degenerates 0-4, shells 71-92, fill 108-630, prune 693-1834, assemble 297-351 ms. What remains in orientation is its global decision: the edge table build (86-106 ms), partners and clusters (55-64), the column grid it waits on (68-113), the parity samples (122-165 sampled, 28-81 refined) and the component, seam-tree and area passes (110-150); cutting those is M3.

Pruning rays measured (2026-11-02), IMG_4113: round 0 judges 998k faces and casts 760k rays (35k faces cast; a blocked face must cast all 25 of its hemisphere rays) walking 35.4M tree nodes in ~375 ms; round 1 judges 135k faces with 705k rays (19.7M nodes, ~200 ms), mostly blocked faces re-testing their 25 rays against the changed faces; rounds 2-9 cast 480-560k rays each but walk 1-8M nodes (16-70 ms). Every ray is needed for the same answers, so only cheaper rays remain: a binned surface-area-heuristic tree cut node visits 12% (35.4M -> 31.1M) and left round 0's time unchanged (368 vs 378 ms), so it was removed again. No code change kept from this step.

Hole triangulation restricted to 3D Delaunay edges tried and dropped (2026-11-02): compared on every loop over 200 edges in IMG_4110, 4113, 4116, 4117 and 4118 (19 loops), the minimum-area search limited to chords that are edges of the loop's 3D Delaunay tetrahedralization (Ixdar's DelaunayTriangulation3D) or its sides found no triangulation on 16 of them, IMG_4117's 1337-edge loop included, so it would fall back to the full search almost always; it also cost more than the full search on most (the Bowyer-Watson there checks every tetrahedron per point), and where it found one it matched the full optimum twice and was worse once (0.00136 vs 0.00074). Thin, twisted scan loops are the case the restriction fails on. Code removed; MeshHoleFiller unchanged.

Cold profile and experiments (2026-11-02). All ten scans cold vs warm (one JVM): orientation 680-870 vs ~225 ms, pruning 690-1765 vs 270-1260, assembly 290-350 vs ~100, fill 80-625 vs 17-375, split+shells 150-310 vs 70-90. JFR on a cold IMG_4113: parity lines (TriangleBvh.faceRange) 278 samples, pruning rays 277, hole filling 121 (79 of them in a boxed TimSort inside MeshHoleFiller.relax). Kept: hole relaxation sorts (key, position) pairs packed in one long with a primitive sort (same order); the minimum-area search skips a split whose two halves already cost the best so far (areas are never negative, so the same triangulation); the ray tree packs sibling boxes and each leaf's triangle coordinates contiguously for the any-hit and winding walks (same floats, round 0 375 -> 343 ms); round 0 tries the two winding rays before the 25-ray hemisphere where parity cannot vouch, as later rounds already do (zero-flip check 0/0/0 on all ten; IMG_4113 exposed 3554 -> 3553, pruned 34889 -> 34878, all others identical); the column grid counts and files in separate loops. Tried and dropped: 64-face ray tasks and 16-triangle leaves (no change: round 0 scales only 1.7x from 2 to 16 threads), packed parity coordinates (the packing costs as much cold as it saves), 128-face orientation clusters (the cold cost moved from the sampled to the refined pass). Finding: about half the cold time is the JIT's latency on each big loop (interpreted until compiled, plus 280-350 deoptimizations per repair, mostly unstable_if from data-dependent branches); it does not shrink with less work. With CPU changes alone the cold floor looks near 2 s on IMG_4113. Moving parity lines and pruning rays to GPU compute would bypass it, but Ixdar has no compute-shader plumbing and its WebGL backend has none; decision with the user.
